definition: At a moment of high impact or energy release, insert a frame (or short run of frames) that abandons the shot's normal color palette entirely for a near-monochrome black-and-white image dominated by sharp, straight lines radiating outward from a central point (a 'starburst' pattern) — explicitly labeled on-screen in this source as a 'HIGH CONTRAST FRAME' — shown recurring across multiple different anime sources credited to the same key animator, suggesting a recognized, named professional technique rather than a one-off effect.
purpose: Sell the intensity of an impact or energy release by briefly breaking the shot's own established color and rendering language, using a starkly different (near-monochrome, radiating-line) visual register that reads as more intense than continuing the shot's normal look ever could.
visible_effect: A frame or short burst of frames showing a stark black-and-white radiating spike/line pattern emanating from a central point, cutting in at the peak of an impact, energy attack, or explosion, then returning to the shot's normal color rendering immediately after.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: Not confirmable from the sampled frames alone (no transcript was available for this video — see evidence_status); visually, the technique's placement at each clip's most intense, highest-energy beat is consistent with a readability/impact-emphasis purpose, matching this batch's own already-documented impact/exaggeration vocabulary, but no spoken claim from the source could be captured to confirm the intended psychological mechanism directly.
physical_interpretation: None — an explicit, stylized departure from the shot's own established rendering, not a claim about the effect's real appearance.
use_cases: the peak instant of a high-energy attack, explosion, or impact in an action sequence, where a shot's established color rendering can be deliberately broken for one beat to sell extra intensity

a personal or small-team 2D project wanting the same technique, since (per the frames showing the source's own project) it is achievable with ordinary rough-sketch-to-clean-fill digital ink/paint tools rather than requiring a large studio pipeline
non_use_cases: a shot or style that specifically avoids breaking its own established color language, where the technique's whole mechanism (a jarring register break) would work against the intended consistency
a slower, non-impact beat where no sudden intensity spike needs selling
